preamble: Lenition of the voiced palatal stop [ɟ] to the palatal approximant [j] removes the oral closure while keeping the palatal place. The Proto-Slavic reflex of *dj, written *ď and usually reconstructed as a palatal stop [ɟ(ː)], became j in Slovene and in the Kajkavian and Chakavian dialects of Croatian (meja 'border'), against Shtokavian đ (međa), Polish and Slovak dz and East Slavic ž. The phonetic value of *ď is debated (palatal stop or palatalized dental), and the change is confined to the western South Slavic area, so it is rare.

examples.note: Compare Serbo-Croatian mèđa, Russian межа́, Polish miedza.
Compare Bulgarian пре́жда, Russian пря́жа, Polish przędza.
Kajkavian and Chakavian j against Shtokavian međa; the same reflex as Slovene (Matasović 2008, cited in the Kajkavian article).
